entries.alt: The Settings screen: the section list grouped by category on the left, with a search box above it, and the Identities section on the right.
The Settings screen after typing "image" in Search settings: the list keeps only the matching sections, followed by the matching setting rows.
The Settings screen in a narrow window: the section list is replaced by a button that shows the current section, Identities.
The two buttons at the bottom of the sidebar: Settings, with the sliders icon, and Log out.
The section list: Search settings on top, then the Account, Mail, Interface, Integrations and About groups with their sections.
The Settings screen on Linked mailboxes, with markers 1 to 5 on the five sections of the Account category in the section list.
The Mailbox preferences card of Linked mailboxes: Use linked mailboxes, Preload linked mailboxes and Show mailbox connection icons.
The form that links a mailbox: username or email address, password, optional display name, and the Verify and link button.
The Provider connection card: a provider choice between Microsoft Graph and Gmail API, an application client ID, and Connect securely.
The Identities list with two identities, the first marked Default, and markers 1 to 4 on the buttons of the second.
The New identity form with Basics, Reply handling, Signature and Sending options groups.
The Signatures list with two signatures, one marked as the default.
The New signature form with a name field, a format choice and the signature text.
The Change password card: current password, new password and confirmation fields, and the password rule.
The Two-factor authentication, Authenticator app and Passkeys cards, before anything is set up.
The Sign-in country policy card with its policy choice, allowed countries and allowed addresses, and the Countries seen card.
The Session security notices card, empty, above the Alert preferences card.
The Active sessions card: the linked-mailbox origin choice, a search box, the session table and the button that signs out the other sessions.
The Sign-in history card with a result filter, Refresh and Export history.
The Remembered devices card with a device name field and the Remember this device button.
The Encryption tab: the Zero-access storage card with its state, the list of what the server still sees, the caveat, and the key setup choice between passphrase and passkey.
The Privacy card of Message content: remote content choice, tracking switches, image retry and unsafe HTML handling.
The Original message HTML card and the Trusted link domains card, with its domain list and subdomain option.
The Trusted link senders card: a list of sender addresses and a list of sender domains, each with a save button.
The Optional usage counts card with one checkbox, off.
The Load times card with two measuring switches and the Error reports card with one switch.
The What we hold about you table: each kind of data this server keeps, how many items, how long it is kept and who handles it.
The Take your data or leave card with Download my data, Restrict use of my data and Delete my account.
The data request form: a request type, optional details and Submit request, above the list of your requests.
The Settings screen on Message display, with markers 1 to 9 on the nine sections of the Mail category in the section list.
The Text and colors card with message colors, font size, line height, reading width and zoom, and below it the Loading and Message header cards.
The Actions and attachments card: collapse attachments by default, the message action ribbon style and the attachment density.
The top of the Message reader actions card: a search box, a preview of the actions ribbon and the first rows that place each action on the toolbar, in the More menu or hide it.
The Flag for follow-up card: a list of reminder presets, each with a checkbox, a name, the next reminder time and buttons to reorder and remove it.
The Attachments bar card and the Attachment previews card with their switches and choices.
The top of the Message badges card: each badge can be set to Always, Only when notable or Never.
The People and contact pictures card and the Save contacts from messages card.
The top of the Cached mail card: the session cache switches, age and size limits, and the Clear cached mail now button.
The Addressing and replies card: whether From is shown, which identity replies use, quick reply, recipient entry and the reply header style.
The Checks before sending card: how to react to invalid recipients, a missing attachment and an empty subject, and the external recipient warning.
The Images in replies card: whether replies and forwards carry the original images, and the trusted sender domains.
The Defaults for new messages card: where the composer opens, receipts, record message opens, signature position and forwarding format.
The top of the Composer features card: a profile choice with Apply profile, and the first group of features with a switch each.
The Sending options, Undo send and Account drafts cards.
The Message notices card with the Enable notices switch and the New notice button.
The Response templates card: use and sidebar switches, a search box, the template count and the Add template button.
The Folder list and order card: every folder with its visibility, unread and total counts, location and actions.
The Folders and sidebar card and the Counter bubbles card.
The top of the Workspace view properties card: visibility, display name and item count for each workspace view.
The Arrange folders card: dragging, nesting behaviour, where new folders appear and drag handles.
The Special folders card: one choice per mail role, each set to Automatic discovery.
The Focused inbox card with its switch, and the Manage Focused senders list.
The Properties, priority and export card: priority marks, the Properties dialogs and their keyboard shortcut.
The Storage card, which says the mailbox does not provide storage usage.
The top of Retention: the last run, the undo window, what this server allows and the list of your rules.
The Folder defaults card: one choice per folder, each set to Inherit, with the Drafts folder marked as protected by the administrator.
The Labels list: a search box and the labels Work, Personal, Important, Later and Receipts with their keyword and colour.
The Builder tab of Mail rules with a new rule open for editing, above the notice that vacation replies are unavailable.
The Raw Sieve tab: the script list, the source editor and the Validate script, Save, Activate and Delete buttons.
The Saved searches section: the default search scope and the New search folder button.
The Read receipts section: delivery notification defaults, how read receipt requests are answered and sender exceptions.
The Import and export mail section with the Import mail button.
The Settings screen on Appearance, with markers 1 to 4 on the four sections of the Interface category in the section list.
The Theme and switching card with the theme choices, and the Colours card with accent and unread badge colour.
The top of the Text and layout card: density, interface font, font size and weight, colours, and message list choices.
The Toolbars card with a pinned or auto-hide choice for four bars, and the Import and export preferences card.
The Shortcut preset card: the Mailwoman, Gmail, Outlook, Vim and Off presets, and the View preset bindings list.
The top of the Offline cache card: offline access, persistent storage, header window, bodies, attachments and cache budget.
The top of the Keyboard shortcuts card: two switches, a search box and a list of actions with their bindings.
The Message selection and moving card and the Mail features card.
The top of the New mail tab: the Notifications and Permission on this device cards and the first New-mail channels.
The Other notification events card and the Toast appearance and behaviour card.
The Background notifications on this browser card: the mailbox chooser and the Register background notifications and Remove for this account buttons.
The Quiet hours card with its switch and the Rules card with Manage notification rules.
The Language and region, Region date and time formats and Time zones cards.
The Settings screen on Nextcloud accounts, with markers 1 to 3 on the three sections of the Integrations category in the section list.
The Nextcloud accounts section with an instance approved by the administrator and the form to link your account.
The Package tracking section when the administrator has not configured a provider: the privacy note and the unavailable notice.
The API keys card with the Create key form open: a label, capabilities, surface, accounts, folders and constraints.
The MCP keys card: a label, a checkbox for each tool, and the Create MCP key button.
The Settings screen on About Mailwoman, with markers 1 and 2 on the two sections of the About category in the section list.
The About Mailwoman section: version, source revision, release tag, build target, support end date and the software inventory downloads.
The Server information section, which says that annotations are read-only for this account.
